identification: Oil on board or canvas, portrait format, framed in a modern gilt moulding with grey linen slip. Evening/dusk bush river scene: tall dead eucalypts with hanging bark at left, dense bush, yellow sunset band, still water with reflections in the foreground. Catalogue: ERNEST CHRISTMAS ATTRIBUTED OIL EVENING ON THE YARRA RIVER H-35 W-25 CM. Style (dark tonal bush river at dusk, gold sky band) is consistent with the late Victorian Australian bush-river genre that Ernest William Christmas (1863-1918, born Adelaide, worked Victoria/NSW, then NZ and Hawaii) painted, but it is a common genre. Ernest Christmas was not a Tasmanian painter, the lot note has that wrong.

viewing_check: Look hard (with a torch, angled) at the lower left and lower right corners for E W C or E.W. Christmas and a date like /90 to /95. Check the back for a label, inscription 'Evening on the Yarra' or a dealer stamp, the board or canvas type (period academy board or 1890s canvas, not modern hardboard), and craquelure consistent with 130 years. If initials and a period support are there, A$200 max; if nothing, cap at A$60-80.
